subject.title: Feishu plugin: remove dependency on contact:contact.base:readonly for sender name resolution

question: Should Feishu basic inbound messaging stop using contact-directory APIs by default, and if so what explicit opt-in contract should remain for sender display names and live user directory listing?
rationale: The source-level issue is valid, but changing the default affects security posture, display-name quality, operator permissions, and existing users who rely on contact-backed names; repository policy treats fallback/default/config changes as maintainer-sensitive.

options.title: Make contact-free the default
options.body: Default inbound sender attribution and `channel-list` peer discovery to contact-free paths, with explicit documented opt-in for contact API lookup and tests for the fallback behavior.

options.title: Keep the opt-out model
options.body: Leave `resolveSenderNames` default-on and document `resolveSenderNames: false` plus permission requirements more prominently, accepting the broader permission dependency for friendly names.

options.title: Defer to display-name PR first
options.body: Resolve the overlapping Feishu display-name PR, then revisit this issue only for the remaining contact-directory default and live directory listing semantics.

recommendation.title: Make contact-free the default
recommendation.body: Default inbound sender attribution and `channel-list` peer discovery to contact-free paths, with explicit documented opt-in for contact API lookup and tests for the fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the current assignee and own the overlapping open Feishu display-name PR, so they are the best available routing point for the permission/default decision.
